## Detailed entries

### Ada

- **Type:** Village
- **Status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** 2026-04-07 (Village Council adopted Resolution 2026-101, amended from 12 to 6 months, 5-0; per approved minutes). Extended 2026-09-01 by Resolution 2026-109 (6-0) for an additional 12 months.
- **Normalized date:** `2026-04-07` (exact)
- **Duration:** Originally six months (to Oct. 7, 2026); extended by an additional twelve months from the effective date of Resolution 2026-109 (emergency, adopted Sept. 1, 2026)
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, cryptocurrency mining
- **Moratorium ID:** `oh-ada-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Village of Ada Resolution 2026-101 (emergency) imposing a temporary moratorium on data centers and cryptocurrency mining centers; extended by Resolution 2026-109 (emergency)
- **What prompted it:** Precautionary: residents' concerns; no inquiries received; village infrastructure cannot supply large data centers; time to write zoning.
- **Affected projects:** None; no companies have shown interest.
- **Detailed status:** Extended as of 2026-09-23; six-month moratorium adopted 2026-04-07 (set to expire 2026-10-07) was extended 2026-09-01 by Resolution 2026-109 for 12 months (to about 2027-09-01). Planning Commission public hearing on legislation to prohibit data centers is set for 2026-09-29.
- **Outcome:** Village pursuing permanent legislation that would prohibit data centers (Planning Commission hearing Sept. 29, 2026).

### Alliance

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-07-06 (City Council meeting)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-07-06` (exact)
- **Duration:** 18 months (not to exceed)
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `oh-alliance-2026`
- **Legal basis:** City Council ordinance/legislation approved 5-1 (Councilman Phillip Mastroianni opposed; Councilwoman Jennifer Kiko absent), denying permits for any 'AI data centers' within city limits.
- **What prompted it:** Councilwoman Sheila Cherry pushed for the pause to protect residents, separate facts from rumors, and to amend related I-2 industrial-district restrictions to include conditional uses; comes after Mayor Andy Grove revealed at least one company had expressed interest in bringing a data center to the city, and follows separate mid-June 2026 legislation restricting future data centers to I-2 industrial zones.
- **Affected projects:** No specific developer/project named in coverage; Mayor Andy Grove said at least one company has expressed interest in bringing a data center to the city.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-07-31 (adopted 2026-07-06); a sub-committee on data centers was formed for future workshops and public discussion.
- **Outcome:** Pending; sub-committee formed to develop conditional-use standards for the existing I-2 industrial-district restriction adopted in mid-June 2026.

### Amherst

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟡 Pending
- **Date enacted:** Pending: Building and Lands Committee unanimously recommended the moratorium legislation to full City Council on 2026-09-22; next council meeting 2026-09-28
- **Normalized date:** `—` (unverified)
- **Duration:** As written: until June 30, 2027 with an automatic six-month extension (council members discussed removing the automatic extension)
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `oh-amherst-undated`
- **Legal basis:** Proposed City of Amherst (Lorain County) legislation (sponsored by Ward 1 Council member Brian Dembinski) prohibiting data centers larger than 2.5 MW during zoning review
- **What prompted it:** Opposition to a proposed 45-megawatt data center at the Nordson property, which needed a zoning variance (BZA hearing, late July 2026); industrial zoning code review underway.
- **Affected projects:** Proposed 45 MW data center at the Nordson property (variance rejected by the Board of Zoning Appeals).
- **Detailed status:** Pending as of 2026-09-23: recommended by the Building and Lands Committee on 2026-09-22; headed to full City Council (meeting 2026-09-28). [VERIFY instrument number; adoption date; primary source (news-only evidence) not confirmed at confidence 0.6 in the 2026-09 refresh]
- **Outcome:** Pause on data centers above 2.5 MW while the industrial zoning code review committee updates regulations.

### Archbold

- **Type:** Village
- **Status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** 2026-04-06 (emergency ordinance); Council had initially tabled a broader proposal on 2026-02-16 following resident pushback and legal hesitation from the Village Law Director and County Farm Bureau, then adopted a narrower six-month moratorium on 2026-04-06
- **Normalized date:** `2026-04-06` (exact)
- **Duration:** 6 months (Resolution 2026-16, 2026-04-06), extended six months by Resolution 2026-27 (emergency, 2026-08-17) to 2027-04-06
- **Current end date:** `2027-04-06`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `oh-archbold-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Resolution No. 2026-16 (temporary moratorium on data centers, advanced manufacturing facilities and technology storage facilities, adopted 2026-04-06, emergency); amended/extended by Resolution 2026-27 (emergency, 2026-08-17)
- **What prompted it:** Resident concern over land off County Road C and possible data center industrialization
- **Affected projects:** No formal project confirmed by village officials in captured reporting
- **Detailed status:** Extended; active as of 2026-09-23 through 2027-04-06 under Resolution 2026-27 (adopted 2026-08-17 as an emergency). A draft zoning amendment by consultant Reveille, Ltd. is complete; planning commission review pending.
- **Outcome:** Council adopted the moratorium unanimously (5 of 6 members present, Council President Karla Ball absent) on 2026-04-06, despite the Village Law Director advising it was unnecessary (no pending applications) and the Farm Bureau warning of litigation exposure.

### Ashtabula Township

- **Type:** Township
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-06-10 (Board of Trustees Wednesday meeting, per Star Beacon story of Friday 2026-06-12; date inferred from 'at a Wednesday meeting')

### Athens

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-08-03 (City Council regular session; rules suspended and Ordinance 0-70-26 unanimously adopted as emergency, per Athens County Independent and WOUB)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-08-03` (exact)
- **Duration:** One year; the mayor and/or service-safety director may extend it one more year
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `oh-athens-2026`
- **Legal basis:** City of Athens Ordinance 70-26 (0-70-26), temporary moratorium on data centers (AI and large-scale data storage), emergency measure
- **What prompted it:** A New York developer (Saadia Holding LLC) is eyeing about 300 acres in Athens and Dover townships across U.S. 33 from Athens High School. The city has no data center zoning standards. Energy, water and air-quality concerns were raised.
- **Affected projects:** Proposed Saadia Holding data center site on U.S. 33 is outside city limits (not directly covered).
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23; one-year moratorium adopted 2026-08-03 runs to about 2027-08-03, extendable one year administratively.
- **Outcome:** City to hire a consultant to assess data center impacts and amend the zoning code.

### Athens Township (Athens County)

- **Type:** Township
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-08-01 (Board of Trustees special session, Saturday; Resolution 08-01-2026 adopted unanimously)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-08-01` (exact)
- **Duration:** 12 months from the effective date, unless repealed earlier or superseded by zoning amendments
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `oh-athens-township-athens-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Athens Township Trustees Resolution 08-01-2026, temporary moratorium on receipt, processing or approval of zoning certificate applications for data center development in the zoned portion of the township (The Plains), under R.C. 519.02
- **What prompted it:** A New York developer is considering about 300 acres on U.S. 33 across from Athens High School, in Athens and Dover townships. The zoning code does not address data centers.
- **Affected projects:** Proposed data center (New York developer, reported as Saadia Holding LLC) on about 300 acres along U.S. 33 across from Athens High School. Part of that land is in unzoned areas.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23; 12-month moratorium adopted 2026-08-01 runs to about 2027-08-01 (applies to the zoned portion of the township).
- **Outcome:** Zoning Commission directed to study and draft data center amendments (districts, setbacks, noise, water, electrical, generators, decommissioning).

### Aurora

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-06-30 (City Council, Ordinance 2026-117, rules suspended and adopted 6-0 as an emergency; per official minutes)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-06-30` (exact)
- **Duration:** Twelve months from the effective date, or until code amendments are enacted or council revokes it, whichever comes first.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `oh-aurora-2026`

- **What prompted it:** Precaution: the zoning code does not permit data centers, but the administration wanted time for a zoning-code consultant to review whether more rules are needed; regional Portage County data center controversy.
- **Affected projects:** None named.

- **Outcome:** City to study and possibly adopt data center regulations as part of its zoning code review.

### Avon Lake

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-06-22 (City Council regular meeting, Monday; per Medina Gazette/Chronicle-Telegram report of 2026-06-26)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-06-22` (exact)
- **Duration:** One year, up to June 22, 2027; council may shorten
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `oh-avon-lake-2026`
- **Legal basis:** City of Avon Lake Ordinance 26-60, a one-year moratorium on the development or construction of data centers
- **What prompted it:** The zoning code has no data center definition, so a facility would fall under general industrial use. The council president cited aggressive data center developers entering Ohio communities, and the legislature had not acted.
- **Affected projects:** None named.

- **Outcome:** Study, plan and draft data center regulations, possibly making data centers a conditional use needing Planning Commission and council review; build an economic development strategy.

### Barberton

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2025-11-10 (City Council, emergency; per 'Passed November 10, 2025' on the legislation and Akron.com report)
- **Normalized date:** `2025-11-10` (exact)
- **Duration:** Indefinite (no end date); on 2026-04-13 data centers were also added to the city's 'various businesses' moratorium, which lasts until adoption of the new Barberton zoning code
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `oh-barberton-2025`
- **Legal basis:** Resolution/Ordinance No. 157-2025 (emergency) instituting a moratorium on data centers within Barberton; later Ordinance No. 50-2026 (passed 2026-04-13) amending Resolution 164-2023 to add data centers to the moratorium on zoning permits until adoption of the new zoning code
- **What prompted it:** Response to Norton's data center controversy (Quantum HPC 'Project Triton'); council said Barberton has little open land and data centers do not contribute to economic development; wanted time to add data center rules after the new development code is adopted.
- **Affected projects:** None in Barberton; prompted by Quantum HPC's proposal in neighboring Norton.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23; open-ended moratorium adopted 2025-11-10 (No. 157-2025), reinforced 2026-04-13 by No. 50-2026 which holds data center zoning permits until the new zoning code is adopted.
- **Outcome:** Council imposed an indefinite moratorium, intending to add data center regulations to its new development code and then cancel the moratorium; in April 2026 folded data centers into its broader zoning-permit moratorium pending the new code.

### Village of Ashville

- **Type:** Village
- **Status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** 2025-12-22
- **Normalized date:** `2025-12-22` (unverified)
- **Duration:** 180 days (Ord. 2025-13, originally recorded 2025-12-22 to 2026-06-20), followed by a second 180-day moratorium under Ordinance 2026-14 (adopted 2026-07-06), through approximately 2027-01-02
- **Current end date:** `2027-01-02`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `oh-ashville-2025`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance 2025-13; extended by Ordinance 2026-14 (adopted 2026-07-06 as an emergency measure, readings waived)
- **What prompted it:** Proposed EdgeConneX project, resident opposition, infrastructure and zoning capacity concerns
- **Affected projects:** Proposed EdgeConneX data center near Ashville
- **Detailed status:** Extended via Ordinance 2026-14, adopted as an emergency measure at the 2026-07-06 Council meeting, imposing another 180-day moratorium (through approximately 2027-01-02); succeeds the original Ordinance 2025-13 (expired 2026-06-20). Active as of 2026-09-23; unaffected by the separate dispute below over the EdgeConneX development agreement. Separately, the underlying EdgeConneX development agreement (Resolution 06-2026, adopted 2026-04-06 as an emergency measure and exempted from the village's own data center moratorium) remains contested. The Ohio Supreme Court ruled 2026-08-07 (State ex rel. McNamara-Smith v. Grube) that Ashville's fiscal officer improperly refused to certify a citizen referendum petition against Resolution 06-2026 because the emergency declaration was not adequately justified; the Pickaway County Board of Elections then voted unanimously to place the referendum on the 2026-11-03 general-election ballot. Village Council subsequently introduced Resolution 16-2026 to repeal Resolution 06-2026 outright and moot the referendum; a 2026-09-08 motion to waive the second and third readings and pass it immediately fell short of the five-vote supermajority required (final tally of 4 in favor, after Mayor Clark broke an initial 3-3 tie, which the council's own rules held insufficient), and at the 2026-09-21 meeting Council instead advanced the repeal to a third reading scheduled for 2026-10-05. As of 2026-09-23, Resolution 06-2026 has not been repealed and the referendum remains scheduled for the November ballot.
- **Outcome:** Resolution 06-2026 authorized a development/consultant-funding agreement (Term Summary, Exhibit A) with EdgeConneX/PowerConneX, allocating $39,300 for GAI Consultants' independent technical review of the proposed project. It did not repeal the moratorium, which was instead independently extended by Ordinance 2026-14 on 2026-07-06. As of 2026-09-23, Resolution 06-2026 itself remains legally intact but contested: the Ohio Supreme Court ordered the village to certify a citizen referendum against it (decided 2026-08-07), the referendum is on the 2026-11-03 ballot, and a Council attempt to repeal Resolution 06-2026 and moot that vote (Resolution 16-2026) has twice failed to gather the votes needed to advance quickly and is now set for a third reading on 2026-10-05.

- **Normalized date:** `2026-06-25` (exact)
- **Duration:** One year
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `oh-xenia-2026`
- **Legal basis:** City of Xenia ordinance (number not found) establishing a one-year moratorium on applications to establish, construct or convert buildings for data centers
- **What prompted it:** Precautionary: nearby Wilmington and Urbana fights; concerns about electric rates, water, noise and heat; zoning code does not address data centers. City had been approached before but grid could not support one.
- **Affected projects:** None active.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23; one-year moratorium passed 2026-06-25 (effective about 2026-07-25) runs to about 2027-07-25.
- **Outcome:** Council to consider zoning regulations for small, medium and large data centers through the planning commission.

### Yellow Springs

- **Type:** Village
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-05-18 (emergency reading)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-05-18` (exact)
- **Duration:** 12 months, expiring 2027-05-18
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `oh-yellow-springs-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Village Council emergency ordinance; Ordinance 2026-08
- **What prompted it:** Pause on zoning permits/approvals for new data centers with aggregate monthly demand or peak load above 2 MW, and for expansions of existing facilities crossing that threshold; council narrowed the proposal at a May 4 work session before adopting it May 18
- **Affected projects:** —
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-07-31; runs through 2027-05-18 unless repealed or replaced earlier
- **Outcome:** Adopted by emergency reading; bars zoning permits/approvals for new or expanded data centers above 2 MW aggregate demand for 12 months, with exemptions for auxiliary data centers and applications/permits already submitted or issued
